item.title: Russian envoy says visit to Iran aimed at averting return to war
item.description: Russia's top diplomat is visiting Tehran for the first time since the U.S. launched its war with Iran, aiming, he says, to avert a return to major hostilities.

item.title: Candidate for Lt. Gov. Shawn Oliver arrested, suspends campaign
item.description: Shawn Oliver, a New Bedford City Councilor and Republican candidate for lieutenant governor, suspended his campaign after he was arrested early Sunday morning.

item.title: Trump spurs states to dump laws regulating new hospitals
item.description: The Trump administration has tied billions in rural health funding for states partly to the policy commitments they make, including ending their certificate of need, or CON, laws governing the construction of new hospitals.

item.title: Trump says Zelenskyy doesn't want to end Russia's war on Ukraine
item.description: As Ukraine and Russia continue trading strikes, Trump accuses Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war sparked by Putin's ongoing full-scale invasion.

item.title: Air Force member dies in rappelling incident at UT San Antonio football game
item.description: A service member was injured and later died after falling while rappelling from the ceiling of the University of Texas at San Antonio football stadium on Saturday.

item.title: Cindy Crawford and family break silence on Presley Gerber's death
item.description: Cindy Crawford, Rande Gerber and their daughter, Kaia, have broken their silence for the first time since Presley Gerber's death​ last month.

item.title: Trudy weakens to Category 1 storm after dumping heavy rain on Mexico
item.description: Trudy was expected to turn toward the west-northwest Sunday night into Monday, taking it away from Mexico's coast and south of the Baja California Peninsula on Monday and Tuesday.

item.title: Expedition to find Amelia Earhart's missing plane comes up empty
item.description: The researchers said what they had hoped was the plane was "likely a collection of large trees" that had washed away, leaving a "single Y-shaped segment."

item.title: Canadian high school footballers cross U.S. border to play alongside American teammates
item.description: High school students from small towns of Sunburst, Montana, and Milk River, Alberta, have joined forces and are uniting fans from both countries.

item.title: Could Kansas elect its first Democrat to Senate since 1932?
item.description: President Trump will return to the campaign trail on Monday in Kansas, a red state, with the midterms fast approaching. Polls there show Republican Sen. Roger Marshall one point behind Democrat Adam Hamilton. Caitlin Huey Burns has more.

item.title: Pope Leo says he will resume activities after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV​ thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday, one day after being discharged from the hospital for cancer surgery.

item.title: Pope Leo leads Sunday prayer days after returning from cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo has returned to the Vatican after his lung cancer surgery sent shock waves through the Catholic church. Chris Livesay reports on what the pontiff had to say during his Sunday service.

item.title: Boy among 2 killed after truck drives onto Wichita soccer field
item.description: A 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed during a soccer game at Stryker Soccer Complex in Wichita, Kansas, according to police.

item.title: 2 killed after pickup truck plows through Wichita field during youth soccer game
item.description: Police in Wichita, Kansas, are investigating why the driver of a pickup truck sped onto a youth soccer field, killing a man and a 6-year-old boy. Ian Lee has the latest.

item.title: U.S. Airman dies after rappelling incident at UT San Antonio football game
item.description: A member of the U.S. Air Force was injured and later died after he fell while rappelling from the ceiling of the Alamodome stadium in San Antonio, Texas, on Saturday.

item.title: 4 dead after large fire breaks out at Canadian military base, officials say
item.description: Canada's defense minister said four service members were killed, and dozens of others were wounded, in an incident at a military base that caused a major fire.

item.title: 4 Canadian service members killed in Alberta military base incident that sparked large fire
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the large fire that broke out at a Canadian military base one of the worst peacetime tragedies for the country's military.

item.title: More than 1,800 arrested in France after protester violence erupts
item.description: Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.

item.title: Anti-government protests explode in France
item.description: Around half a million people took part in marches across France over poor school conditions and high cost of living, but they were overshadowed by what President Emmanuel Macron called "unrestrained violence" by "insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals." Aidan Stretch is in Paris with the details.

item.title: Trump defends shifting positions on Ukraine, touts progress with Russia
item.description: As President Trump touted "great progress" being made with Russia to end the conflict it started with Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that the U.S. siding with Russia would be a "historic mistake." Taurean Small reports from West Palm Beach, Florida.

item.title: Majority of Americans think U.S. economy is on the "wrong track"
item.description: Americans say they are feeling the pain of the rising cost of living, and they are not optimistic the U.S. economy is on the right track. Akiko Jujita is in Los Angeles with more.

item.title: Allegations of potential noncitizen voting spark legal fights
item.description: With early voting for the midterms underway, federal actions around the U.S. voting system are expanding. Election officials explain their response, and the Justice Department says "there should be no interruption" with the results.

item.title: Helium, critical for tech, faces supply chain crisis
item.description: The war in Iran is threatening the world's supply of helium, a natural resource crucial for a range of industries.

item.title: Election officials describe federal government's actions around the voting system | 60 Minutes
item.description: Election officials respond to allegations from the Justice Department about noncitizen voting as new polling shows that only half of Americans believe the upcoming elections will be free and fair.

item.title: Helium, key for semiconductor manufacturing and medical equipment, faces shortage | 60 Minutes
item.description: Helium, most closely associated with party balloons, but critical for far more, is facing supply chain issues due to the war with Iran. The shortage has left American industry desperate for answers.

item.title: Sacha Baron Cohen: The 60 Minutes Interview
item.description: Actor Sacha Baron Cohen breaks down his iconic characters: Ali G, Bruno and Borat. He also explains the complexities behind his brand of undercover comedy.

item.title: Sebastian Junger on Ukraine war | 60 Minutes
item.description: Having recently returned from Ukraine, new 60 Minutes contributor Sebastian Junger discusses the stakes of President Trump's new diesel deal with Russia.

item.title: 10/18/2026: The Vote; Up in the Air; Sacha Baron Cohen
item.description: First, federal actions around voting system expand. Then, why you should care about a helium shortage. And, Sacha Baron Cohen: The 60 Minutes Interview.

item.title: 10/18: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Americans pessimistic about economic outlook, polls show. Trump defends position on Russia and Ukraine.

item.title: Iran says offer, conditions to reopen Strait of Hormuz still on
item.description: Iran's foreign minister said the U.S. could see the strategic waterway open within days if it abided by the conditions presented in the seven-day ceasefire plan.
